name: Open Science Framework
tagline: A free, open platform for researchers to collaborate and share their work
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on Center for Open Science for operational funding
awards: Recognition as leading open science infrastructure by UNESCO
Featured in multiple research transparency initiatives
policy_outcomes: Influenced NIH and NSF open science policies
Adopted by major research institutions for reproducibility standards
documented_limitations: Limited adoption in some non-English speaking regions
curation_criteria: Community-driven with Center for Open Science oversight; projects must comply with open science principles and data sharing guidelines
contributor_governance: Open contribution model with community review; governance by Center for Open Science board
disparity_tracking: Limited formal tracking; efforts to increase accessibility in Global South
community_ownership: Shared governance between Center for Open Science and research community
controversies: Debates over mandatory data sharing requirements
Discussions about privacy protections for sensitive research
legal_regulatory_issues: GDPR compliance considerations for international researcher data
government_partnerships: NIH collaboration on open science standards
ai_involvement: Limited; basic recommendation systems for project discovery
political_relevance_summary: OSF addresses the reproducibility crisis in science and barriers to research transparency. By making research open and replicable, it strengthens the evidence base available for public policy decisions.

movement_building_utility.notes: Open Science Framework provides foundational data infrastructure, standards, or platforms that other civic technology efforts build upon.

generalizability_notes: High generalizability. Open Science Framework is open source and already deployed across multiple countries/jurisdictions, making replication straightforward for other contexts.
